payload.title: AI Builders Daily · 2026-06-16
payload.summary:
**Anthropic** pushes managed agents into self-editing mode with dreaming and multiagent orchestration; **OpenAI** researcher **Dan Roberts** says reinforcement learning plus test-time compute is turning models into engines for scientific discovery; **Vercel**, **Replit**, and **Google** all ship harder toward agentic products, longer runtimes, specialist agents, and 70+ language voice input; meanwhile builders on X keep the tone volatile, mixing tool obsession, regulation fights, and a lot of very online product takes.

**Anthropic**把托管代理往前推了一截，dreaming、outcomes、多代理编排一口气放出来；**OpenAI** 的 **Dan Roberts** 讲得很直，RL 加测试时算力，已经开始摸到“模型自己做发现”这件事；产品层面也没闲着，**Vercel** 拉长函数运行时，**Replit** 继续押注垂类代理，**Google** 把语音输入扩到 70 多种语言；X 上还是那个熟悉的 builder 气味，一边晒爽点，一边吵开源、监管，还有人已经从 VC 往一线跑了。

items.person_name: The MAD Podcast with Matt Turck

sections.headline: **OpenAI’s Dan Roberts** says reasoning + RL may turn AI into a discovery engine / **OpenAI** 的 **Dan Roberts** 说，推理加 RL 正把 AI 往“发现引擎”上推
sections.body:
On **The MAD Podcast**, **Dan Roberts** argues the big shift is not a single magic moment but a smooth climb driven by reinforcement learning, test-time compute, and models that can stay on a hard problem long enough to find something non-obvious. He points to **o1**-style reasoning as the clearest public marker so far, and says that in science and math the interesting jump is persistence: models can now explore contrarian paths instead of only polishing familiar ones.

He also contrasts **OpenAI**’s recent math work with **Google DeepMind**’s formal-proof route in **Lean**. Roberts’ framing is that AI science will arrive gradually, through systems that become useful in more parts of the research loop before they ever look like fully autonomous scientists.

在 **The MAD Podcast** 里，**Dan Roberts** 的判断很明确：这不是某个神奇时刻突然发生的飞跃，而是一条持续上升的线，背后靠的是强化学习、测试时算力，还有模型愿意在难题上硬啃更久。他把 **o1** 式推理看作目前最清楚的公开信号，尤其在科学和数学里，真正变有意思的是“韧性”这件事，模型不只是修修补补熟路子，已经会往反常识的方向试。

他还拿 **OpenAI** 和 **Google DeepMind** 的数学路线做了对照：前者更像开放探索，后者更偏 **Lean** 里的形式化证明。Roberts 的核心意思不是“科学家 AI 明天就来了”，而是研究流程里越来越多环节，模型已经开始真正派上用场。

sections.headline: **Claude Managed Agents** adds dreaming, outcomes, and multiagent orchestration / **Claude Managed Agents** 上线 dreaming、outcomes 和多代理编排
sections.body:
**Anthropic** is extending **Claude Managed Agents** in three directions at once: dreaming to review past sessions and rewrite memory, outcomes to grade work against a rubric and trigger retries, and multiagent orchestration so a lead agent can split jobs across specialists on a shared filesystem. The pitch is simple: less babysitting, more self-correction, and better handling of long, messy tasks.

The blog also comes with concrete benchmark-style claims. **Outcomes** improved task success by up to 10 points in internal testing, with file generation gains of +8.4% on **docx** and +10.1% on **pptx**. Customer examples are aggressive too: **Harvey** reportedly saw roughly 6x higher completion rates, while **Wisedocs** cut review time by 50%.

**Anthropic** 这次不是补小功能，而是把 **Claude Managed Agents** 往“能自己迭代”的方向推了一大步。dreaming 负责回看历史会话、整理记忆；outcomes 用 rubric 打分，不达标就重来；多代理编排则让主代理把活拆给不同 specialist，在同一个文件系统里并行干活。意思很直白：少盯人，多自纠，复杂脏活也能扛久一点。

它还给了几组挺硬的数字。**Outcomes** 在内部测试里把任务成功率最多拉高 10 个点，生成 **docx** 和 **pptx** 的成绩也分别多了 8.4% 和 10.1%。客户案例更敢写：**Harvey** 说完成率大概涨了 6 倍，**Wisedocs** 说审查速度快了 50%。

sections.headline: Longer **Vercel** function runtimes land on top of **Fluid** compute / 更长的 **Vercel** 函数运行时，背后是 **Fluid** 计算底座
sections.body:
One of our most requested features, longer Vercel function runtime, is here.

What looks like an innocent tweak of a constant… is actually the conclusion a multi-year compute platform investment.

Builds, Sandbox, and now Functions run on our homegrown microVM-based Fluid compute infrastructure.

This investment has enabled innovations like function multi-concurrency, Active CPU pricing, and Secure Compute for private connectivity to existing cloud workloads… with lots more to come, in fact, in the coming days and weeks 😎

我们最常被提的功能之一，更长的 Vercel function 运行时，现在来了。

看上去像只是改了个无害常量……其实是多年计算平台投入的结果。

Builds、Sandbox，现在连 Functions，都跑在我们自研、基于 microVM 的 Fluid 计算基础设施上。

这笔投入已经带来了 function 多并发、Active CPU 定价、还有给现有云工作负载做私有连接的 Secure Compute……而且后面还有更多，真的就是接下来几天几周。😎

sections.headline: Levie says the winners will customize intelligence, not just scale models / Levie 说赢的人靠的不是把模型堆更大，而是把智能做成自己的
sections.body:
Key post that gives a bit of insight into what the future of AI could look like.

“The most interesting thing happening in AI isn't that one model is getting smarter. It's that intelligence is becoming increasingly customizable. The companies that win won't necessarily be the ones with the biggest models. They'll be the ones that turn intelligence into something uniquely their own.”

The ability to combine your unique data, workflows, and a layer that can route intelligence to whatever model best performs the task is clearly the future.

这条帖子挺能说明 AI 未来大概会长什么样。

“AI 里最有意思的变化，不是某一个模型变得更聪明了，而是智能正在变得越来越可定制。最后赢的公司，不一定是模型最大的那家，而是能把智能真正做成自己东西的那家。”

把你自己的数据、工作流，再加上一层能把任务路由到最合适模型的系统拼起来，这显然就是接下来的方向。

sections.headline: Levie argues AI regulation should focus on uses, not every model release / Levie 认为监管该盯应用风险，不该卡死每一次模型发布
sections.body:
It’s very easy to say “we need an FDA for AI” or some equivalent government agency. Well this is what that would look like.

The capabilities of AI models have near infinite permutations. It’s going to be very hard have a purely objective set of metrics that can be universally applied before every model release, without extended back and forth, research, and debate between model labs, academics, and the government. 

Now, imagine this same process with every country that you’re doing business with, globally, for every single model release. Add in a backlog of dozens of AI model releases, and you can quickly see how in the limit this will dramatically slow down all AI progress. 

This is why we need to primarily focus on regulating the applied uses of AI, where the risk actually shows up.

嘴上说“我们需要一个 AI 版 FDA”或者类似机构很容易。那真做出来，大概就是下面这样。

AI 模型的能力组合几乎是无限的。想在每次模型发布前，都拿出一套纯客观、还能普遍套用的指标，基本注定会陷进模型实验室、学界和政府之间没完没了的拉扯、研究和争论。

再想想，如果你在全球多个国家做业务，每次模型发布都要重复这一整套流程。再叠上几十个模型版本排队，你很快就会发现，这样搞下去，AI 进展会被明显拖慢。

所以监管重点应该主要放在 AI 的实际使用场景上，因为风险真正冒出来的地方在那里。

sections.headline: Nikunj says VCs are heading back to operating, faster than before / Nikunj 说 VC 正在加速回到一线做事
sections.body:
I now know 32 VCs who have moved back to operating in the last 12 months.. everyone from associates to GPs. 

Maybe it’s this way all the time and I’m just noticing it, but the pace seems to be accelerating. And they seem much much happier? 

From a professional perspective, it makes sense especially if you are junior. You get to work directly with customers and work as a team. A lot more autonomy than having to pander to GPs. 

From a compensation perspective too, why wait for carry for 13 years when you can have a chance of liquidity a lot sooner. 

As someone who had been operating for a while but loving venture rn, I completely get the trade. To the remaining players, see you on the field 🫡

过去 12 个月里，我已经知道有 32 个 VC 回去做一线运营了……从 associates 到 GPs 都有。

也许一直都这样，只是我现在才注意到，但这个速度看起来确实在变快。而且他们看上去开心多了？

从职业角度看，这很说得通，尤其如果你还比较 junior。你可以直接面对客户，也能跟团队一起干活。比起一直迎合 GPs，自主性高太多。

从收入角度也一样，既然有机会更早拿到流动性，为什么还要为了 carry 等 13 年。

我是那种做过一线、现在也挺喜欢做 venture 的人，所以我完全理解这个选择。还留在场上的各位，球场见 🫡
